### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A02 opened 96 of 200 traces (about 48 in 100) and the pair A06+A12 the other 104 (about 52 in 100); the two entry options never mixed — A02 never co-occurred with A06 or A12, while A06 and A12 always came together. In the later window, A02, A06 and A12 each occur in all 200 traces: A02 and A12 once per trace, A06 about twice per trace (mean ~2.1, the same as before when it occurred). [OCC002, OCC006, OCC012, REL019, REL025, REL071]
- In the later window the opening is a fixed sequence: about 90 in 100 of A02's observed outgoing transitions lead to A06 (before, A02 led to A03 in about 56 in 100 and A07 in about 44 in 100, never to A06), A02 precedes A12 in about 97 in 100 traces, and A12 still passes on to A03 or A07 as before; A11, previously present in about 26 in 100 traces (always alongside A06), now appears in about 53 in 100. [DIR002, DIR006, DIR010, REL025, OCC011, REL070, POS002]
- The detour through the enlarged opening pushed the core loop later: A03 and A07 now follow A02 at a distance of 3–5 steps (previously 1–2) and their median relative positions moved from about 0.39/0.40 to about 0.50/0.49, while the loop's internal routing (A03, A04, A05, A07 and their successors) is essentially unchanged. [LAG001, LAG004, POS003, POS007, DIR003, DIR004, DIR007]
- A01 is new: it was not observed in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces) and occurs exactly once in every trace in the later window, near the end (median relative position about 0.94). [OCC001, POS001]
- A01 is wired into the closing A15/A16 segment. Before, A15 and A16 led only to each other, always at distance 1; in the later window, A15 and A16 each send about half of their observed outgoing transitions to A01, A01's observed successors are A16 (about 54 in 100) and A15 (about 46 in 100), direct A15↔A16 successions now sit at distance 2 in about 35–37 in 100 cases, and A05 gained a new edge to A01 (about 17 in 100 of its outgoing transitions). [DIR011, DIR012, DIR001, LAG082, LAG083, DIR005]
- The route from the core loop to the closing block lengthened: A03, A05, A07 and A14 now reach A15/A16 about one to two steps later than before. [LAG019, LAG020, LAG030, LAG031, LAG048, LAG049, LAG080, LAG081]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the process opening was restructured around A02, A06 and A12: where the earlier window had two alternative entry paths (A02 alone, or A06 together with A12, in roughly equal shares, never combined), the later window runs a single mandatory opening in which A02 — now at the very start of every trace — leads to A06, A06 recurs about twice and passes to A11 (about half of its outgoing transitions) or A12 (most of the rest), and A12 feeds the essentially unchanged A03/A07 core loop. This is shown directly by the flip from perfect mutual exclusivity to universal co-occurrence between A02 and A06/A12, the rerouting of A02's transitions to A06, the doubling of A11's presence always alongside A06, and the lengthening of the A02→A03/A07 distances, while the loop's own branching shares barely moved. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012, DIR002, DIR006, DIR010, REL019, REL025, REL071, LAG001, LAG004, POS002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR007]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is residual variant behaviour within the later window: about 10 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions still bypass A06 (leading to A12, A07, A11 or A03), and the exact internal order of the repeated A06/A11 block is not resolved, so the later window may mix the new standard opening with leftover old-style cases; with 200 traces per window, these sub-patterns rest on limited support. [DIR002, DIR006, DIR009, DIR010]

Other differences: A01 was added as a new activity executed exactly once per trace near the end, wired into the closing A15/A16 segment — A15 and A16 now pass to A01 in about half of their outgoing transitions, A01 returns to A15/A16, their mutual distance is 2 in about 35–37 in 100 cases, and A03/A05/A07/A14 reach A15/A16 one to two steps later; separately, A05 and A14 occur slightly less often (means down about 0.25 each) and A08/A13 participation slipped from about 37 to 33 in 100 traces, the latter a weak signal. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR005, DIR011, DIR012, LAG019, LAG030, LAG048, LAG080, LAG082, LAG083, OCC005, OCC014, OCC008, OCC013]
